claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to gather a bit more detail about Alex and your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?** (I need this to determine if he falls within the eligible age range for Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 17 earlier this year. Let me think... his birthday is in March, so he was born in March 2008.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually just left school recently. He's signed up with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next - you know, getting some guidance on his options for the future.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Before I can make my final assessment, I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I'm giving you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I can now make my assessment.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex has just left school and is now signed up with the careers service, he would be eligible for a 20-week continuation of Child Benefit from the date he registered with the careers service.

Let me confirm one final detail to complete my assessment:

**Did Alex register with the careers service within 20 weeks of leaving school?** (This will help me confirm whether you're still within the eligible period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he registered pretty much right after he left school. It's only been a few weeks since he finished.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need to make my assessment. Let me provide you with my final decision:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's the summary:

- **Alex's eligibility: Yes** ✓
- Alex is 17 and lives with you, which meets the basic requirements
- He has recently left school and registered with a government-sponsored careers service
- The rules allow you to claim Child Benefit for 20 weeks from the date he registered with the careers service
- Since he registered just a few weeks ago, you are well within this 20-week window

**Important reminder:** This 20-week eligibility period is from the date Alex registered with the careers service. After those 20 weeks, your eligibility will end unless his circumstances change (for example, if he enters approved education or training).

You should apply for Child Benefit as soon as possible if you haven't already done so!
